source_refs.note: Exercise 1.3, Question 7: Exercise 1.3 questions, book page 11

blocks.prompt: 7 Find a polynomial of degree 4 with zeros \(2i,\ -2i,\ 1,\ -1\), and satisfying \(P(2)=240\).
blocks.explanation: We build a polynomial from its zeros: each zero \(r\) gives a factor \((z-r)\), and \(P(z)=a(z-z_{1})(z-z_{2})\cdots\) with an unknown number \(a\) in front. The extra condition fixes \(a\). Then expand and check.
steps:
Step 1: Write the factors and pair them
\[P(z)=a(z-2i)(z+2i)(z-1)(z+1)\]
\[=a(z^{2}+4)(z^{2}-1)\]
Why: Each pair is a difference of squares: \((z-2i)(z+2i)=z^{2}+4\), \((z-1)(z+1)=z^{2}-1\).

Check: P(2)
\[10(16)+30(4)-40=240\]
Why: The condition holds.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (page 297) prints this answer under the label 6, as \(x=10z^{4}+30z^{2}-40\). It is the answer to Question 7, and it should read \(P(z)=\) rather than \(x=\). The polynomial itself is correct.
